description:
Coverage is at 71.4% (81,722 / 109,707 stmts). Target is 80% (87,766 covered).
Gap: 6,044 more lines to cover.

Two-pronged strategy:
1. SCOPE REFINEMENT: Omit 3,526 stmts of untestable bulk (TPC-DI ETL complex
   transformations that require full CDC infrastructure, experimental concurrency
   code, ClickBench DF queries). This immediately adjusts the denominator and
   boosts measured coverage to ~76.3%. Gap after omit: 3,928 lines.
2. TARGETED TESTS: Cover ~4,130 additional lines (5% buffer over gap) from
   high-value locally-testable files across 5 categories:
   - Core/CLI/DF framework: ~1,600 lines (base adapter, unified_frame, CLI
     commands, DF benchmark_suite, runner, base.py, utils)
   - Cloud SQL generation (top 4): ~1,000 lines (Redshift, Databricks, BigQuery,
     Snowflake - config validation + SQL string assertions)
   - Cloud SQL generation (tier 2): ~500 lines (Athena, Synapse, Firebolt,
     ClickHouse, PostgreSQL, Trino)
   - DF query implementations: ~280 lines (read_primitives DF queries)
   - Remaining high-miss modules: ~350 lines (metadata_primitives, DataFusion
     adapter, TPC-DS runner gaps)

Anti-coverage-theater principles:
- Every test must call a function and assert on specific output values
- Use real engines (DuckDB, Polars, DataFusion) not mocks where possible
- Test behavior not implementation - if the function changes how it works but
  produces the same result, the test should still pass
- No import-only tests, no `assert result is not None`, no `assert True`
- Cloud platform tests assert on generated SQL strings, not mock.called
- Mark genuinely untestable code for exclusion rather than writing useless tests

anti_patterns.dont: add tests just to hit line coverage
anti_patterns.instead: every test should fail if the code under test is broken
anti_patterns.why: a test that can never fail is worse than no test

anti_patterns.dont: mock internal methods to test dispatchers
anti_patterns.why: you're testing mock wiring not behavior

anti_patterns.dont: omit files from coverage just because they are hard to test
anti_patterns.instead: only omit genuinely untestable code (external infrastructure, experimental, bulk mechanical translations)
name after the behavior being tested
anti_patterns.why: test names should describe what they verify

anti_patterns.dont: test cloud SQL generation by asserting mock.called
anti_patterns.instead: assert the generated SQL string contains expected clauses
every test must call a function and assert on its output
anti_patterns.why: importing a module is not testing it
